main_text.p: extra caluam pofitis, nulla ad articulos uiȧ est, qua tenuis ille humor ad ofsium conne xiones ac copagines ferri possit. Duƈtus enim, quibus humores ab una sede, aut pluribus in alias prouehi queant, nerui funt, aut uenæ & arteriæ. Sed ab ijs exterioribus capitis partibus nulli inseruntur nerui: habent enim omnes suam originem à cerebri substantia. Deinde illinc nullę magnæ promanant uenæ & arteriæ, quæ ad ipsos desi-nant articulos. Huc accedit quòd simplex pituita & pura in uenis & arteriis nũquam consistit, sed extra ea uasa semper gignitur ac continetur. Igitur ab ijs partibus extra caluam sitis nulla arthritidis materia ad articulos fertur. Quapropter defluxionis origo, uel ab ipso cerebro est, aut ab eius finibus, aut ab hepate & uenis. Interdu ê cerebro per foramen nucæ intra tendonum tunicas defluit pituita per spinam dorsi in articulos per neruos, quæ per coanã, uel per nares, aut per palatum expurgari debuerat. Talem autem defluxionem præcedit capitis grauitas & ceruicis, quæ interdum uel frigus, uel horrorem inducit. Quòd autem à uisceribus, & intimis partibus arthritidis materia emanet, ostendit Hippocr. Aphorismo

page.notes: Catchword "rifmo" is the continuation of "Aphorismo" (printed "Apho-" / "rifmo" split across the line end). Ligature/long-s forms are normalised to plain s. Two spelling-related items left as printed: "Interdu ê" (the ê is a printed abbreviation/mark, likely "Interdum" with a superscript mark, uncertain) and "coanã" (macron as printed). Lines in the image are slightly tilted; the reading is from the scan and some letters at the edges (e.g. "dorsi") are uncertain and may warrant checking.
